assumptions: Interview is in approximately seven days.
Daily availability was not provided; this plan assumes up to four focused hours per day, with a total of approximately 27.5 hours. Reduce the workload if that is not realistic.

For an entry-level role, coding problem-solving is expected to be the main technical focus. System-design depth varies by company and interview loop, so this plan covers fundamentals and communication rather than advanced architecture.
Resource links are general study references, not claims about requirements at any particular company.
roadmap_overview.overall_strategy: Spend most time solving and explaining common coding problems, prioritizing arrays, strings, hash maps, and reusable algorithm patterns. Build tree and graph fundamentals after core coding practice. Learn a lightweight system-design framework and apply it to one small service. Finish with timed practice, behavioral preparation, and targeted review. Use an error log to direct the final study sessions.

priority_distribution.rationale: Coding interviews are a central entry-level technical screen at many companies. Practice on high-frequency patterns has the broadest expected impact.
You report little system-design experience, so a focused foundation can help without displacing core coding preparation.

schedule.adjustment_strategy: The plan assumes up to four focused hours daily. If you have less time, preserve the timed coding mock, T2 practice, and system-design framework; remove optional extra problems first. If you discover a major coding gap, shift time from additional system-design detail or new patterns to independent coding practice and review. If your recruiter confirms there is no system-design round, reduce T5 to a brief fundamentals review and spend that time on your weakest coding pattern. Include short breaks within study blocks; they are not counted as focused study hours.

readiness_benchmarks.benchmark: On an unfamiliar coding prompt, clarify requirements, explain an approach before coding, and communicate progress and trade-offs.
readiness_benchmarks.measurement_method: Use the timed mock or record a practice session; check whether each step occurred without a reminder.
readiness_benchmarks.target_threshold: Complete all five steps in at least one mock: clarify, propose, analyze, implement, and test.
readiness_benchmarks.remediation_if_unmet: Practice narrating the five-step routine on two easier problems before attempting another timed mock.

readiness_benchmarks.benchmark: Solve representative array, hash-map, and common-pattern problems independently.
readiness_benchmarks.measurement_method: Track a set of fresh timed problems, including whether the final solution passes self-created normal and edge-case tests.
readiness_benchmarks.target_threshold: As a practical readiness target, solve at least 3 of 4 representative easy or medium problems independently within about 30 to 40 minutes each, with correct complexity analysis.
readiness_benchmarks.remediation_if_unmet: Identify whether failures come from pattern recognition, implementation, or edge cases; drill the weakest category and retry with new problems.

readiness_benchmarks.benchmark: Implement basic tree DFS, tree BFS, and graph traversal with appropriate state tracking.
readiness_benchmarks.measurement_method: Write implementations from a blank editor and explain complexity and visited-state behavior.
readiness_benchmarks.target_threshold: Correctly implement at least one DFS and one BFS traversal without consulting a solution, including relevant empty-input and repeated-visit checks.
readiness_benchmarks.remediation_if_unmet: Trace a small example by hand, review base cases and queue or stack operations, then re-implement from memory.

readiness_benchmarks.benchmark: Structure a small design discussion around requirements, APIs, data, request flow, and trade-offs.
readiness_benchmarks.measurement_method: Deliver a timed 20-minute walkthrough and check each required design element against a checklist.
readiness_benchmarks.target_threshold: Cover requirements and assumptions, at least one API, a basic data model, request flow, one bottleneck, and one trade-off.
readiness_benchmarks.remediation_if_unmet: Use a fixed outline and redo a smaller design prompt; prioritize clarity and justified choices over adding components.

readiness_benchmarks.benchmark: Complete a realistic coding mock while reasoning aloud, testing code, and responding constructively to difficulty.
readiness_benchmarks.measurement_method: Score the mock on correctness, approach, complexity, communication, edge cases, and time management.
readiness_benchmarks.target_threshold: Reach at least 4 of 6 categories at a satisfactory level, with no major communication or testing failure; use this as a planning target rather than a company-specific cutoff.
readiness_benchmarks.remediation_if_unmet: Review the recording or notes, choose the two weakest categories, and perform a shorter focused practice before the interview.

readiness_benchmarks.benchmark: Explain truthful examples of collaboration, challenge, learning, and project contribution.
readiness_benchmarks.measurement_method: Rehearse aloud and check that each answer gives context, your specific actions, and an outcome or lesson.
readiness_benchmarks.target_threshold: Prepare at least four concise examples and a clear explanation of your contribution to each relevant resume project.
readiness_benchmarks.remediation_if_unmet: Draft bullet-point STAR outlines from real experiences and rehearse them without memorizing a script.

technical_interview_approach: Restate the problem and clarify constraints, expected input, output, and edge cases before coding.
Offer a straightforward solution first, then improve it if the constraints justify optimization.
Explain the key invariant or reasoning before implementation.
Write code in the language you know best; keep names clear and avoid unnecessary abstractions.
Use a small example to trace the implementation and test edge cases such as empty input, duplicates, boundaries, and disconnected nodes where relevant.
State time and space complexity and explain the trade-offs.
If stuck, communicate what you know, test a simpler case, and consider a brute-force approach rather than going silent.
behavioral_preparation: Prepare truthful STAR-style examples for collaboration, a difficult problem, a mistake or failure, and learning or initiative.
Keep context brief and emphasize your own actions, decisions, and outcome.
Be ready to discuss how you received feedback, handled uncertainty, and worked with others.
Do not invent metrics or claim ownership of work you did not perform.
project_and_resume_preparation: Review each resume project and prepare a concise explanation of the problem, your contribution, implementation choices, and outcome.
Be prepared to discuss one technical trade-off, one challenge, and what you would improve next.
Review the code or technical details of projects you expect to discuss so your explanation matches your actual work.
common_mistakes_to_avoid: Starting implementation before understanding constraints or explaining a plan.
Optimizing prematurely without first establishing a correct approach.
Ignoring edge cases, testing only one happy path, or failing to state complexity.
Treating a memorized solution as understanding; practice re-implementation from a blank editor.
Overcomplicating an entry-level system design with components that do not follow from requirements.
Spending the final day on advanced topics instead of reviewing mistakes and protecting time for rest.

highest_impact_actions: Complete timed, independent practice on arrays, strings, hash maps, and common patterns, and track mistakes in an error log.
Practice explaining your reasoning and testing edge cases aloud on every problem.
Implement tree DFS, BFS, and basic graph traversal from memory.
Use a simple requirements-first framework to practice one or two small system designs.
Complete one timed mock interview and use its results to choose final review topics.
activities_to_deprioritize: Advanced dynamic programming, specialized graph algorithms, and niche data structures unless your target interview information specifically calls for them.
Deep distributed-systems architecture beyond the basic concepts needed for a small design discussion.
Passive video watching, large unfiltered problem lists, and repeatedly reviewing solutions without re-implementing them.
Learning a new programming language or switching tools during the final week.
final_review_strategy: Review the error log and select only the two or three most consequential weaknesses.
Re-solve previously missed problems from a blank editor and explain the approach before coding.
Refresh complexity analysis, binary-search boundaries, hash-map use, traversal patterns, and edge-case testing.
Rehearse one concise system-design outline and your behavioral and project examples.
On the final evening, stop adding new topics; prioritize light review, logistics, and adequate rest.
final_recommendations.readiness_assessment: Given the unknown starting skill level and only one week, readiness cannot be guaranteed. You are in a stronger position if you meet the independent-coding and timed-mock benchmarks, can implement basic traversals, and can communicate a structured small-system design. If coding benchmarks remain unmet, prioritize coding accuracy and communication over expanding system-design depth.
